access-control.title: Access Control
access-control.description: Access control is a set of security measures that regulate who can access a system, services, data, or resource. Access control policies use authentication and authorization to verify users and enable access.

accuracy.title: Accuracy
accuracy.description: Accuracy measures the degree to which data describes the real-world phenomena it is intended to represent.

api-catalogue.title: API Catalogue
api-catalogue.description: A listing of application programming interfaces and exchange contracts with metadata, intended for use by a software developer.

api-consumer.title: API Consumer
api-consumer.description: An organization, system, service, or application that uses an API to access data or functionality provided by another system or service.

api-gateway.title: API Gateway
api-gateway.description: A technology platform that acts as a single entry point for multiple application programming interfaces, managing requests, routing, security, and other operations, simplifying and centralizing API management.

applicant.title: Applicant
applicant.description: (a) The person named on a land title form as the person acquiring an interest in land. (b) The person named as applicant in the application section is the person with whom land title staff is authorized to communicate with regarding an application.

application-programming-interface-api.title: Application Programming Interface
application-programming-interface-api.description: An Application Programming Interface (API) is a software-to-software interface that provides a secure and standardized way for applications to communicate with each other to deliver requested data without user intervention.

audit-event.title: Audit Event
audit-event.description: A signed, immutable log entry recording access or transfer events.

authentication.title: Authentication
authentication.description: Authentication is a security process for verifying the identity of a user or device before allowing access to a system, resource, or function. Authentication validates that a user or system is who they claim to be.

authentication-type.title: Authentication Type
authentication-type.description: Method used to verify the identity of a user or system, such as passwords, tokens, OAuth, API keys, or multi-factor authentication patterns.

authoritative-data.title: Authoritative Data
authoritative-data.description: Data located in any repository system that is recognized through governance, law, or common acceptance as the source of origin for accurate data on a specific topic. Authoritative Data may be stored or referenced in a Data Register.

authoritative-data-directory.title: Authoritative Data Directory
authoritative-data-directory.description: The publicly accessible list of datasets that are designated authoritative through the corporate data governance process. This information is published in the BC Data Catalogue.

authorization.title: Authorization
authorization.description: Authorization is a security process for providing a user or device with access to a requested system, resource, or function based on permissions. Authorization is provided only after a user or device has been authenticated e.g. IDIR.

authorizing-authority.title: Authorizing Authority
authorizing-authority.description: The entity responsible for confirming that a data exchange has the required legal basis, consent, delegation, or policy authority to proceed.

central-government-agencies.title: Central government agencies
central-government-agencies.description: There are many independent or partially independent agencies, boards and commissions that are essential to effectively governing the province. Agencies include authorities, boards, commissions, corporations and councils. A public agency also includes any bodies established by the government on an interim basis to perform arbitration, regulation or similar functions.

certificate-authority-ca.title: Certificate Authority
certificate-authority-ca.description: A Certificate Authority (CA) is a trusted organization that provides/issues digital certificates to websites, businesses, and individuals. This establishes trust between users and websites by ensuring that sensitive data remains private.

channel.title: Channel
channel.description: The transport mode used for an exchange: Pull API, Push Webhook, Message Queue, Batch File, or Streaming.

child.title: Child
child.description: A resident of B.C. who meets all of the following conditions:Is a child of a beneficiary or a person who stands in place of a parentWho is a minorDoes not have a spouseIs supported by the beneficiary

completeness.title: Completeness
completeness.description: The proportion of stored data against the definition of “100% complete”. Completeness is contextual to the purpose for data collection (for example, is the scope of collection the whole province or a region?)

connected-services-data-dictionary.title: Connected Services Data Dictionary
connected-services-data-dictionary.description: The centralized repository documenting technical metadata for Connected Services data elements.

connected-services-glossary-of-terms.title: Connected Services Glossary of Terms
connected-services-glossary-of-terms.description: The centralized repository documenting concepts in plain language for Connected Services business and technical terms.

consent.title: Consent
consent.description: Consent is a voluntary agreement by an individual for their personal information to be accessed, verified or used by a government service for specified purposes such as determining or verifying eligibility for other benefits or services.

conveyance.title: Conveyance
conveyance.description: A transfer of an estate or interest in land (other than by will) to a new owner through sale, lease, or other means. A transfer of title is the conveyance of an estate or interest in land in exchange for some financial consideration, typically a sale.

copyright.title: Copyright
copyright.description: Copyright is an exclusive legal right to reproduce, publish and sell a work or material. Copyright encompasses a wide range of materials including: written materials, such as books, manuals, reports and computer software; visual materials such as videos, photographs, pictures, posters and maps; and audio materials such as music and voice recordings.

corporation.title: Corporation
corporation.description: A corporation means a company, a body corporate, a body politic and corporate, an incorporated association or a society, however and wherever incorporated, but does not include a municipality or a corporation sole.

credential.title: Credential
credential.description: A verifiable claim about an actor or system used for authentication or authorization.

critical-system.title: Critical System
critical-system.description: Any IM IT service, system, or infrastructure component that is deemed necessary by the System Owner to deliver a Mission Critical Function.

crown-corporations.title: Crown corporations
crown-corporations.description: Crown corporations are owned by the government, but operate at arm’s length from the public service and elected officials.

crown-land.title: Crown Land
crown-land.description: Land owned and administered by a government, either federal or provincial. In British Columbia, Federal (Canadian) Crown land includes National Parks, Indian Reserves, federal ports and military bases. Provincial Crown land includes provincial parks and all ungranted land (wilderness) within the provincial boundaries. Most of British Columbia is Crown land.

data.title: Data
data.description: The smallest meaningful units of recorded information generated by an organization, which gain significance when stored in a structured manner that enables them to be synthesized and interpreted.

data-accessibility.title: Data Accessibility
data-accessibility.description: The ability for authorized users to easily find, retrieve, and use data when they need it, supported by appropriate permissions, usable formats, documentation, and interoperability that allows data to work across systems and contexts.

data-catalogue.title: Data Catalogue
data-catalogue.description: A data catalogue is a listing of data in an organization (e.g., B.C. Data Catalogue) that is designed to help data users quickly find appropriate data for any analytical or business purpose.

data-custodian.title: Data Custodian
data-custodian.description: For the data assigned to them, data custodians provide oversight throughout its lifecycle; ensure intended users of the data are supported and trained appropriately; and the data meets the requirements of applicable laws, policies, and standards.

data-element.title: Data Element
data-element.description: The smallest identifiable unit of data with a defined meaning, typically represented as an attribute or field within a data model or dataset.

data-exchange.title: Data Exchange
data-exchange.description: A governed, repeatable transfer of data from a provider to a consumer under an approved legal basis.

data-minimization-rule.title: Data Minimization Rule
data-minimization-rule.description: Restricts shared data to the minimum required for the purpose.

data-quality.title: Data Quality
data-quality.description: A measure of the data’s reliability, including its accuracy, completeness, timeliness, consistency, validity, uniqueness, and interoperability.

data-quality-assessment-framework.title: Data Quality Assessment Framework
data-quality-assessment-framework.description: Data Quality Assessment Framework defines standardized dimensions of data quality and associated measures for assessing the level of data quality. A measure may apply at the dataset, record, and/or attribute level.

data-quality-scorecard.title: Data Quality Scorecard
data-quality-scorecard.description: A Data Quality Scorecard is an instance or snapshot of a dataset’s data quality measures, as defined by the Data Quality Assessment Framework.

data-register.title: Data Register
data-register.description: A set of data that contains Authoritative Data and follows a specific standard to ensure quality, interoperability, and data sharing.

data-resource.title: Data Resource
data-resource.description: Data Resource (or Resource) for a Data Catalogue is a file containing actual data, uploaded to the Catalogue (e.g. CSV, xls, XML etc.); or relevant information in the Catalogue, describing how to obtain the actual data (e.g. API specification). A data resource is always relevant to a particular Dataset.

data-sharing-agreement-dsa.title: Data Sharing Agreement
data-sharing-agreement-dsa.description: The Data Sharing Agreement (DSA) is a legal agreement defining the lawful basis, permitted use, retention, and custodianship for an exchange.

dataset.title: Dataset
dataset.description: The structured collection of data for a defined topic, for example an entity, domain, or subject area. Dataset refers to the data, metadata about the dataset as well as optionally associated Data Resource/s

delegated-intermediary.title: Delegated Intermediary
delegated-intermediary.description: A system, service, or platform component authorized to act between exchange participants to route, broker, enforce, or transform a data exchange on behalf of a provider or consumer.

delegation.title: Delegation
delegation.description:
Delegation is a secure, formalized process that permits an individual to authorize another individual to access, manage or act on their behalf within digital government services.  
Delegation enables individuals —especially the elderly, persons with disabilities, or those with limited digital literacy—to benefit from digital services without being excluded.

dependant.title: Dependant
dependant.description: In relation to another person, it means anyone who resides with the person and who is the spouse of the other person, or is a dependent child of the person, or indicates a parental role for the person's dependent child.  Note: Adults are not considered to be dependants of each other on the sole basis of demonstrating a parental role towards the same child.

dependent-child.title: Dependent Child
dependent-child.description: With respect to a parent, it means a child, other than a child who is 18 years of age and is a person with disabilities, who resides in the parent's place of residence for more than 50 per cent of each month and relies on that parent for the necessities of life.   In relation to a dependent child, a parent includes but is not limited to: A biological mother or father;  An adoptive mother or father;  A person with legal custody, other than a director under the Child, Family and Community Service Act or an administrator under the Adoption Act;  A person with legal guardianship, other than a director under the Child, Family and Community Service Act or an administrator under the Adoption Act OR  A person who is the parent of the parenting dependent child.A client temporarily caring for a child without legal custody or guardianship may also be considered a parent. Caring for a child may include one or more of the following, but is not limited to:making day-to-day decisions affecting the child;having day-to-day care, control and supervision of the child;making decisions respecting where the child will reside;making decisions respecting the child's education and participation in extracurricular activities;making decisions respecting the child's cultural, linguistic, religious and spiritual upbringing and heritage;applying for a passport, licence, permit, benefit, privilege or other thing for the child;exercising any other responsibilities reasonably necessary to nurture the child's development. Note: Under certain circumstance a dependent child may be excluded from a family unit. For example, when two parents are separated but are residing together and the dependent child resides with both the separated parents 100% of the time.

dependent-post-secondary-student.title: Dependent post-secondary student
dependent-post-secondary-student.description:
A resident of B.C. who meets all of the following conditions:

Older than 18 and younger than 25 years of age

In full-time attendance at a recognized post-secondary institution (this includes trade, technical or high schools)

Supported by a beneficiary who is the person’s parent or who stands in place of the person’s parent

dependents.title: Dependents
dependents.description: Dependents include a spouse, children and dependent post-secondary students.

document.title: Document
document.description: A document refers to any of the land title forms or supporting material (including survey plans) which are submitted as part of an application to register an interest in land within British Columbia. Examples include: title transfers, mortgages and easements.

endpoint.title: Endpoint
endpoint.description: Specific URLs or interfaces in an API or service where requests are sent and responses are returned; the “access points” for interacting with a system.

enterprise-data.title: Enterprise Data
enterprise-data.description: Enterprise data is collected and used across all departments in an organization to support planning, daily operations, and decision‑making. It is governed by processes (Enterprise Data Management) to ensure it is accurate, secure, and accessible for business value.

entity.title: Entity
entity.description: A uniquely identifiable real-world object, event, or concept about which data is stored. Entities are described by attributes and may have relationships with other entities.

equity.title: Equity
equity.description: Equity is the percentage of property value remaining after all charges registered against your property and current year property taxes have been deducted from the current assessed value.

extract-transform-load-etl.title: Extract, Transform, Load
extract-transform-load-etl.description: Extract, Transform, Load (ETL) is a process that extracts, transforms, and loads data from multiple sources to a data warehouse or other unified data repository.

fee-simple.title: Fee Simple
fee-simple.description: Fee Simple is the form of ownership of real property (real estate) in which the owner has the right to control and transfer the property at will.

globally-unique-identifier-guid-universa.title: Universally Unique Identifier
globally-unique-identifier-guid-universa.description: A Universally Unique Identifier (UUID), also called a Globally Unique Identifier (GUID), is a 128‑bit number generated in a way that makes it effectively guaranteed to be unique across different systems and over time, without needing any central coordination.

high-value-data.title: High Value Data
high-value-data.description:
High Value Data holds significant business value, enabling decision-making in support of programs, services, evaluation, and accountability requirements that benefit a high number of users. This includes data that supports critical services or data of public interest or permanent value (e.g., critical information and authoritative data).

The B.C. Data Catalogue only holds High Value Datasets.

immutable.title: Immutable
immutable.description: An element (such as an identifier, data structure, or stored record) is considered immutable when its value or state is fixed at creation and does not change thereafter. Immutability provides a consistent point of reference and supports reliable auditing, versioning, and data integrity, even as related or derived information may evolve.

independent-boards-commissions-and-tribu.title: Independent boards, commissions and tribunals
independent-boards-commissions-and-tribu.description: Independent boards, commissions and tribunals are established by the government to perform arbitration, regulation or similar functions. The provincial government appoints at least one representative to these agencies.

integration.title: Integration
integration.description: The technical implementation that enables an exchange, such as APIs, connectors, or file transfers.

interest-holder.title: Interest Holder
interest-holder.description: A beneficial owner of a relevant trust, a corporate interest holder of a relevant corporation, or a partnership interest holder of a relevant partnership

interest-in-land.title: Interest in Land
interest-in-land.description: As defined in LOTA, this term refers to an estate in fee simple; a life estate in land; a right to occupy land under a lease that has a term of more than 10 years; a right under an agreement for sale to occupy land, or require the transfer of an estate in fee simple.

land-act.title: Land Act
land-act.description: An enactment that provides the statutory framework for the administration of Crown land, establishes the responsibilities of government Ministers regarding the administration of Crown land and provides for the delegation of certain authorities. Many powers have been delegated to the Surveyor General with respect to Crown land definition and disposition.

land-owner-transparency-act.title: Land Owner Transparency Act
land-owner-transparency-act.description: The Land Owner Transparency Act was passed by the government of British Columbia in May 2019. The first-of-its-kind in Canada, it created an accessible registry of beneficial interests in land in B.C. – the Land Owner Transparency Registry.

land-owner-transparency-registry.title: Land Owner Transparency Registry
land-owner-transparency-registry.description: A publicly searchable registry of information about beneficial ownership of land in British Columbia. Beneficial owners are people who own or control land indirectly, such as through a corporation, partnership, or trust. The registry is intended to end hidden ownership of land in BC. The Land Owner Transparency Registry launched November 30, 2020, and opened to public search on April 30, 2021.

land-title-act.title: Land Title Act
land-title-act.description:
A comprehensive 400-section statute that prescribes the legal program under which the land title system operates, the Land Title Act designates:
•	The Director of Land Titles to regulate land title practice.
•	The Registrar(s) of Land Titles as the primary statutory decision maker(s) in the administration of the land title system.
The Land Title Act establishes the land title register and requirements respecting its operation and records.

land-title-register.title: Land Title Register
land-title-register.description: That part of the records of the land title office, including electronic records, where information respecting registered indefeasible titles is stored. It is independently maintained by the LTSA under the statutory authority of the registrars of land titles and in accordance with the requirements of the Land Title Act respecting permanent records retention.

legal-description.title: Legal Description
legal-description.description: A unique identifier for each parcel of land in the province. It is a text description that may include lot number, plan number, survey system identifiers (Range, Block, Township, District Lot, District, etc.) and other text.
legal-description.example: LOT 1, PLAN EPP12345, DISTRICT LOT 123, NEW WESTMINSTER LAND DISTRICT

legal-notations.title: Legal Notations
legal-notations.description: Information recorded against a title to land following the receipt of an application concerning matters other than ownership of interests in land, such as statutory restrictions on use (such as the application of a heritage designation bylaw) or rights relating to other land (such as the existence of an appurtenant easement on the title of adjacent land).

lien.title: Lien
lien.description: An interest in land claimed to secure the payment of a debt or the performance of some other obligation. Examples include Claim of Builders Lien for payment of debt related to labour or materials, Certificate of Lien for payment of strata fees, or Tax Act Liens for payment of various taxes.

master-data.title: Master Data
master-data.description: Core, non-transactional data that describes key business entities (e.g., persons in BC, services, assets, locations). Master Data should represent Authoritative Data so it can be trusted and used with confidence by the entire organization.

metadata.title: Metadata
metadata.description: Metadata is a set of structured data that describes and gives additional detail about a Dataset. Metadata helps identify, manage, and share Datasets.

metadata-record.title: Metadata Record
metadata-record.description:
A Metadata Record is the combination of Description of the Dataset + collection of Metadata attributes / objects / elements; where a Metadata attribute / object / element is any one piece of relevant metadata for the Dataset. 

Core set of metadata attributes / objects / elements are defined in the Metadata Standard.

metadata-template.title: Metadata Template
metadata-template.description:
Metadata Template refers to an electronic capture format for the metadata schema.

The Metadata Schema defines the structure of the metadata; including, amongst others, core mandatory elements / objects / attributes (as defined in the metadata standard) and additional optional elements / objects / attributes.

minimum-viable-dataset.title: Minimum Viable Dataset
minimum-viable-dataset.description: A Minimum Viable Dataset (MVD) contains only data essential to its purpose.  For example, a Parks Names data register only contains data about park names (official name, legal name, pronunciation) and no other park data.

ministries.title: Ministries
ministries.description: The B.C. Public Service is divided into ministries. Each ministry is responsible for a specific area of public policy, government function or service delivery.

mortgage.title: Mortgage
mortgage.description: An interest in land granted by the registered owner (the mortgagor) to a lender (the mortgagee) as security for a debt.

msp-spouse.title: Spouse
msp-spouse.description: A resident of B.C. who is married to or is living and cohabiting in a marriage-like relationship with the applicant.

non-repudiation.title: Non-repudiation
non-repudiation.description: A security principle that ensures a person or system cannot deny having performed a specific action, such as sending a message or approving a transaction - typically achieved through logging, digital signatures, and strong authentication.

open-data.title: Open Data
open-data.description: Data that has undergone an Open Data Assessment and is licensed under the Open Government Licence - British Columbia. Such Open Data is then made available to the public for copying, publishing, distribution, transmission and adaptation under the terms of the OGL-BC.

parcel.title: Parcel
parcel.description: A lot, block or other area in which land is held or into which land is subdivided.

parcel-identifier-pid.title: Parcel Identifier
parcel-identifier-pid.description: Parcel Identifier (PID) is a nine-digit number that uniquely identifies a parcel in the land title register of British Columbia. The registrar assigns PID numbers to parcels for which a title is being entered in the computer register as a registered title. The Land Title Act refers to the PID as the permanent parcel identifier.

personal-health-number.title: Personal Health Number
personal-health-number.description: Each B.C. resident enrolled with the Medical Services Plan (MSP) is given a unique lifetime identifier for health care called a Personal Health Number (PHN). Your PHN remains the same, regardless of any changes to personal status, and can be found on your BC Services Card.

professional-regulatory-authorities.title: Professional regulatory authorities
professional-regulatory-authorities.description: Professional regulatory authorities are government agencies or public organizations with authority delegated by law from the government. They provide oversight and certification to specified regulated occupations in B.C.

program-authority.title: Program Authority
program-authority.description: The ministry, program area, or authorized business function that has the mandate or lawful basis to request, approve, or participate in a data exchange.

property-transfer-tax.title: Property Transfer Tax
property-transfer-tax.description: A tax paid when one purchases or gains an interest in property that is registered at the land title office. The provincial Ministry of Finance is responsible for administering the Property Transfer Tax (PTT).

public-body.title: Public Body
public-body.description: A government-related organization or agency funded to deliver public services to citizens.  For example, a government ministry, central government agency, Crown corporation, or regulator.

public-body-type.title: Public Body Type
public-body-type.description: The category of the public body defined in public bodies definition.

rate-limit.title: Rate Limit
rate-limit.description: A control that defines the maximum number of requests a user, application, or system may make to a service within a specified period.

reference-data.title: Reference Data
reference-data.description: Data that is used to describe or classify other data (e.g., lists of disease types, gender codes, building materials, etc.)

registered-owner.title: Registered Owner
registered-owner.description: A registered owner is the person who owns an interest in land, either in terms of ownership of title in fee simple, or ownership of a charge. A registered owner is recorded in the land title register upon registration.

registrar.title: Registrar
registrar.description: An official keeper or recorder of records. The Registrar is a statutory decision maker under the Land Title Act, and an employee of the LTSA with a statutory responsibility under LOTA to refuse an application to register an interest in land if the transferee fails to submit a transparency declaration with the application and, in the event the transferee is a reporting body fails to submit a transparency report.

registration-number.title: Registration Number
registration-number.description: The unique serial number assigned to each entry in the Land Title Register.

residency.title: Residency
residency.description:
Residency or "Ordinarily resident" in B.C. refers to the place where the applicant or recipient normally lives the regular routine of their day-to-day life. Indicators may include but are not limited to:

•An established “place of residence” in B.C. Learn more by reviewing the support, shelter and special care page
•Residence of spouse, children, and other dependent family members in B.C.
•Legal and other documents indicating B.C. residence, such as utility bills
•B.C. driver's license or BC services card
•Registration of vehicles in B.C.
•Employment or business relationships in B.C.
•Links to community in B.C. through religious organizations, recreational and social clubs, unions, and professional organizations
•Life or health insurance policies in B.C., such as BC Medical Services Plan coverage
•Filing income tax returns as a B.C. resident
•Bank or other financial accounts with a home branch in B.C.
•Applying for government assistance, programs, and/or financial benefits in B.C.
•The frequency, length, purpose, and intention of stays within and outside of B.C.
Repeated instances of leaving BC, returning briefly, and then leaving again would most likely not be considered as ordinarily resident of B.C..

resident.title: Resident
resident.description:
A resident is a person who meets all of the following conditions:

A citizen of Canada or lawfully admitted to Canada for permanent residence

Makes their home in B.C.

Physically present in B.C. at least six months in a calendar year

Eligible B.C. residents (citizens of Canada or persons who are lawfully admitted to Canada for permanent residence) who are outside B.C. for vacation purposes only, are allowed a total absence of up to seven months in a calendar year

scoping-details.title: Scoping Details
scoping-details.description: Information used to determine whether a data exchange is authorized, appropriately limited, and aligned with the intended purpose, participants, and policy requirements.

secure-data-exchange-sdx.title: Secure Data Exchange
secure-data-exchange-sdx.description: Secure Data Exchange (SDX) is a capability/piece of functionality is the ability to move data securely and lawfully between parties. Includes technical patterns, governance, tooling and audit controls.

service.title: Service
service.description: A service represents an external upstream API or microservice consisting of a URL, which listens for incoming requests.

source-of-truth.title: Source of Truth
source-of-truth.description:
A centralized, authoritative location where an organization stores its most accurate, reliable and trusted data, ensuring consistent use of information for decisions, eliminating silos and discrepancies. 

A Source of Truth may be the same as the System of Record, however this may not always be the case. For example, valid authoritative copies of data from the System of Record are created and made available for specific purposes; in cases where the System of Record cannot be directly accessed for legal, technical, privacy or other reasons.

spouse.title: Spouse
spouse.description:
Unmarried couples are considered spouses if they meet either of the following criteria:
1) demonstrate qualities consistent with a marriage-like relationship while residing together for 12 consecutive months, or
2) if they declare that they are in a marriage-like relationship.
Married couples who can demonstrate they have separated are exempted from being considered spouses. 
Separated means that they have legally separated, in divorce 
proceedings, severed financial interdependence or social and familial interdependence, etc.

system-of-record.title: System of Record
system-of-record.description: A System of Record (SoR) is the authoritative source where data for a specific domain is created/collected, maintained, and shared.

system-of-reference.title: System of Reference
system-of-reference.description: A System of Reference (SoRef) is a system that consolidates and harmonizes data from multiple systems of record to provide a trusted reference for sharing data.

timeliness.title: Timeliness
timeliness.description: The degree to which data represent reality from the required point in time. Includes currency (are the data up to date?) and latency (when was the data last updated?)

title.title: Title
title.description: Depending on the context in which it is used title means, on the one hand the right of ownership of land and, on the other, the instruments or evidence of such right. In the register, title to land evidences fee simple ownership of land in one or more Registered Owner(s). Also referred to as land title and indefeasible title. A title may also refer to the ownership of interests in land less than fee simple, such as a mortgage or easement.

title-search.title: Title Search
title-search.description: A record issued by the land title office setting out the particulars of a title to land generated from information contained in the register at a specific point in time.

transaction.title: Transaction
transaction.description: A single instance of an exchange, for example one API call or message delivery.

transfer.title: Transfer
transfer.description: The voluntary act of a registered owner of an interest in land transferring that interest to another person, typically as a consequence of a sale or gift of the land to that person. The term includes a conveyance, a grant and an assignment.

transferee.title: Transferee
transferee.description: An individual or corporation to whom an interest in land is transferred. Includes a grantee, an assignee and a person entitled by transmission to be a registered owner of an interest in land.

transferor.title: Transferor
transferor.description: An individual or corporation transferring an interest in land to another party.

transmission.title: Transmission
transmission.description: A change of ownership of land consequent on death, sale under execution, order of court or other act of law, or on any testamentary settlement or legal succession in the case of intestacy.

transparency-declaration.title: Transparency Declaration
transparency-declaration.description: A declaration that is filed by each transferee together with an application to register an interest in land, stating whether the transferee is a reporting body, and, if the transferee is a reporting body, whether the reporting body is a relevant corporation, a trustee or a relevant trust, or a partner of a relevant partnership. Transparency declarations may also be filed at any time, independently of an application to register an interest in land to correct information contained in a previously filed transparency declaration.

transparency-report.title: Transparency Report
transparency-report.description: A report that is filed with a transparency declaration on an application to register an interest in land, if the transferee is a reporting body. The transparency report contains information about the reporting body and its interest holder(s).

trust-authority.title: Trust Authority
trust-authority.description: The governing body (Connected Services B.C.) that manages trust anchors, certificates, and federation governance.

uniqueness.title: Uniqueness
uniqueness.description: The degree to which there are no duplicate data.

validity.title: Validity
validity.description: The degree to which data conforms to its defined domain of values, including the rules for allowed formats, structures, acceptable ranges, and lists of permissible values.
